pages.page_summary: The page concludes a previous section on a pendulum (calculating velocity at B and ratio of kinetic energies at B and C) and begins Section 5.9 on the potential energy of a spring. It introduces Hooke's Law (Fs = -kx), defines the spring constant k, and derives the work done by a spring force (Ws = -kxm^2/2) using integration and graphical area analysis.
knowledge_points: The velocity at point B is vB = √(3gL).
The ratio of kinetic energies at points B and C is KB/KC = 3/1.
At point C, the string becomes slack and the velocity of the bob is horizontal and to the left.
If the string is cut at point C, the bob executes projectile motion with horizontal projection.
The spring force is an example of a variable force which is conservative.
In an ideal spring, the spring force Fs is proportional to displacement x from the equilibrium position.
Hooke's law is mathematically stated as Fs = -kx.
The constant k is called the spring constant and its unit is N m⁻¹.
A spring is stiff if k is large and soft if k is small.
The work done by the spring force for an extension xm is Ws = -kxm²/2.
The work done by the spring force can be obtained by considering the area of the triangle in the Fs vs x plot.
